p1.en: To investigate a topic carefully to gather information

p1.ex1: Scientists do research in order to find better solutions.

p1.en: To bake and prepare a cake from ingredients

p1.ex1: Can you teach me how to make a chocolate cake?
p1.ex2: He made a special cake for the big celebration.

p1.ex1: It is finally time for us to make a firm decision.
p1.ex2: He made a brave decision to set up his own business.

p1.en: To offer an idea for someone else to consider or try

p1.ex1: She made a very helpful suggestion to improve the plan.
p1.ex2: He made a practical suggestion to improve the recipe.

p1.en: To try hard to do something, especially when it is difficult
p1.example: She makes a real effort to improve her skills daily.
p1.ex1: You need to make more effort during your lessons.
p1.ex2: He made a genuine effort to arrive on time.

p1.en: To give a reason — often a false one — for not doing something
p1.example: He always makes excuses when he arrives late.
p1.ex1: Please don't make an excuse — just apologise directly.
p1.ex2: She made a weak excuse to avoid attending the meeting.

p1.en: To form new friendships and relationships with people
p1.example: She always found it very easy to make new friends.
p1.ex1: Making friends in a completely new city takes time.
p1.ex2: He made friends quickly when he joined the new class.

p1.en: To decide in advance what you are going to do
p1.example: They made exciting plans to visit the new restaurant.
p1.ex1: She made careful plans for the big celebration.
p1.ex2: Let us make plans together for this coming weekend.

p2.en: A wide road in a city, often with trees; used in street names

p2.ex2: They brought up their children in a small country cottage.

p2.en: The direction in which the sun rises each morning

p1.en: Very unusual, surprising, or remarkable

p1.ex2: The view from the cliff top was quite extraordinary.

p1.en: A space or opening between two things or in something

p1.en: The solid surface of the earth that you stand and walk on

p1.ex1: She sat comfortably on the ground near the warm campfire.
p1.ex2: The expedition team searched the ground carefully for footprints.

p1.ex1: The cliff was absolutely huge and very impressive to see.

p1.en: To try to find something or someone by searching

p1.ex1: She started to look for the campsite on the map.
p1.ex2: The professor was looking for unusual footprints in the mud.

p1.ex1: She was lost and could not find her way to the campsite.
p1.ex2: He used the sign to help lost travellers find the path.

p1.en: Soft, wet earth or soil, especially after rain
p1.example: The creature's large footprints were clearly visible in the mud.
p1.ex1: Her boots were completely covered in thick, heavy mud.
p1.ex2: The ground was full of deep mud after the heavy rain.

p1.en: Not wide; having only a small distance from one side to the other

p1.ex2: The narrow old bridge was quite difficult and scary to cross.

p1.en: To say you are willing to give or do something for someone

p1.ex1: She offered to carry the heavy equipment up the cliff.
p1.ex2: He offered the lost and tired hiker some food and water.

p1.en: To aim your finger at something to show where it is

p1.ex1: He pointed at the massive creature standing near the cliff.
p1.ex2: The sign pointed clearly to the direction of the campsite.

p1.en: A senior teacher at a university; a title used before their name

p1.ex1: Professor Smith was the first to discover the unusual footprints.
p1.ex2: She greatly admired the professor's impressive knowledge and courage.

p1.en: To arrive at a place after travelling; to manage to get somewhere

p1.ex1: She was completely exhausted when she finally reached the top.
p1.ex2: It took three long days to reach the remote valley.

p1.en: A journalist who investigates and presents news stories for the public
p1.example: The reporter photographed the mysterious footprints in the mud.
p1.ex1: She was a brave reporter investigating the dangerous expedition.
p1.ex2: The reporter was amazed by everything she discovered there.

p1.en: A large, solid and hard piece of stone
p1.example: She carefully climbed the huge rock near the steep cliff.
p1.ex1: He slipped badly on a wet rock during the long hike.
p1.ex2: The creature was hiding silently behind a very large rock.

p1.en: To prepare and arrange something so it is ready to use
p1.example: They quickly set up the tent at the campsite before dark.
p1.ex1: She efficiently set up camp right beside the river.
p1.ex2: The professor set up a major expedition to find the creature.

p1.en: To produce or reflect a bright and clear light

p1.ex2: There was absolutely no sign of the creature anywhere.

p1.ex1: The view from the very top of the cliff was extraordinary.
p1.ex2: They set up their camp near the top of the mountain.

p2.ex2: According to the reporter, the expedition was a great success.

p2.en: Feeling slightly angry or irritated because of something

p2.ex1: He felt very annoyed by the bad weather ruining the trip.
p2.ex2: The professor was annoyed by the reporter's constant questions.

p2.ex2: She found his repeated questions very annoying.

p2.ex2: They were shocked and surprised when they came second.

p2.en: An organised event in which people try to win by being the best

p2.en: Making you feel sad because it is not as good as you expected
p2.example: The weather during the trip was really very disappointing.
p2.ex1: Losing the competition by such a small gap was very disappointing.
p2.ex2: It was disappointing not to reach the top of the cliff.

p2.en: Feeling uncomfortable, ashamed or self-conscious in a social situation

p2.en: Causing you to feel uncomfortable, ashamed or self-conscious

p2.en: Making you feel extremely tired after a lot of effort

p2.ex1: Climbing the steep cliff was physically and mentally exhausting.
p2.ex2: She found the long and difficult hike really exhausting.

p2.ex2: The children were frightened by the strange mysterious sign.

p2.en: Causing you to feel afraid, scared or worried

p2.ex2: She found the dark and narrow mountain path very frightening.

p2.en: An informal and relaxed social meeting or party with friends

p2.ex2: Go-karting can be tiring but is incredibly fun and exciting.

p2.en: The solid surface of the earth; an area of ground

p2.ex2: The land near the cliff was narrow, rocky and difficult to walk on.

p2.en: A written announcement giving information or instructions to the public

p2.ex2: The professor put up a notice about the important expedition.

p2.en: A special container for items such as bottles and paper to be recycled

p2.en: Feeling calm, comfortable and free from stress or worry

p2.en: Feeling frightened or afraid of something or someone

p2.ex2: They were scared by the enormous creature's mysterious footprints.

p2.en: Causing you to feel frightened or afraid
p2.example: The narrow path running along the cliff edge was really scary.
p2.ex1: It was very scary to be completely lost in the dark forest.
p2.ex2: She found the creature's huge and strange footprints very scary.

p2.en: Feeling very surprised and upset by something unexpected
p2.example: She was shocked to see just how deep the narrow valley was.
p2.ex1: He was shocked when he came last in the important competition.
p2.ex2: They were shocked by the completely extraordinary and unexpected news.

p2.en: Very surprising, upsetting or difficult to believe
p2.example: It was shocking to discover such huge footprints in the mud.
p2.ex1: The reporter wrote a truly shocking story about the expedition.
p2.ex2: She found the terrible state of the campsite absolutely shocking.

p2.en: Causing surprise because it is not what you expected

p2.en: To join in and participate actively in an activity or event

p2.ex2: Everyone was warmly encouraged to take part in the get-together.

p2.en: Making you feel tired after doing it for a period of time
p2.example: The long journey to the remote campsite was really tiring.

p2.ex2: She found the competition much more tiring than she had expected.

p1.en: many times; repeatedly without stopping

p1.ex2: The headteacher had to explain the rules again and again.

p1.en: constantly; at every moment without exception

p1.en: to have a disagreement with someone using angry words

p1.ex2: In the past, teachers were much stricter than they are today.

p1.en: a heated disagreement between two or more people

p1.ex2: The argument was solved when they both agreed to discuss calmly.

p1.en: to feel concern or interest about someone or something

p1.ex2: He doesn't care about the argument — he just wants to fix things.

p1.ex2: The school play included a part for every class.

p1.en: to have an effect on someone's behaviour or decisions

p1.en: information, facts or understanding gained through experience or education

p1.en: something remembered from the past; also the ability to remember

p1.en: to respond to something that has happened

p1.en: to take the place of something or someone

p2.ex2: She told him to take it easy instead of arguing again and again.

p1.ex1: Junk food contains a harmful amount of fatty and salty items — bad for vision.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, the amount of junk food on sale has grown — going on a diet is essential.

p1.en: harmful or unfavourable in effect
p1.example: Junk food has a negative effect on heart health and vision.
p1.ex1: Nowadays, a diet rich in fatty and salty food has a negative effect on sight.
p1.ex2: She noticed a negative amount of vitamins in the items she bought — all junk food.

p1.en: at the present time; in the current period
p1.example: Nowadays, junk food contains a harmful amount of fatty and salty items.
p1.ex1: Nowadays, going on a diet rich in vitamins and fibre has a positive effect on sight.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, the amount of fresh produce on sale appears to grow year by year.

p1.en: to make or grow something; to cause something to happen
p1.example: A diet rich in vitamins allows the body to produce energy and maintain good vision.
p1.ex1: Fresh vegetables grown locally produce more fibre than processed junk food items.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, harmful fatty food produces negative effects on the heart and sight.

p1.en: to become heavier; to gain body weight
p1.example: She was putting on weight by eating junk food — she decided to go on a diet.
p1.ex1: Cutting down on fatty and salty items helped her stop putting on weight.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, eating a large amount of junk food causes people to put on weight quickly.

p1.en: the total amount or number of something
p1.example: The quantity of vitamins in fresh food is higher than in junk food items.
p1.ex1: She cut down on the quantity of salty and fatty food and noticed a positive effect on her heart.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, the quantity of junk food on sale is harmful to public health and vision.

p1.en: containing a large amount of a particular substance
p1.example: A diet rich in vitamins and fibre has a positive effect on vision and heart health.
p1.ex1: Fresh produce grown locally is rich in fibre — much better than junk food items.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, going on a diet rich in vitamins allows the body to produce energy healthily.

p1.en: the activity of selling; also an event when items are sold at reduced prices
p1.example: Nowadays, junk food items on sale contain a harmful amount of fatty and salty substances.
p1.ex1: The quantity of fresh produce on sale has grown — a positive effect on public diet.
p1.ex2: She noticed that bitter and sour items on sale contained more vitamins than junk food.

p1.en: containing or tasting of salt
p1.example: Cutting down on salty and fatty food has a positive effect on heart health.
p1.ex1: Junk food items on sale are often salty and contain a harmful amount of additives.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, salty food is known to have a negative effect on vision and the heart.

p1.en: the ability to see; also something seen
p1.example: A diet rich in vitamins has a positive effect on sight and overall vision.
p1.ex1: Cutting down on junk food allows the body to maintain good sight in the dark.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, the harmful effect of fatty food on sight and vision is well documented.

p1.en: having a sharp acid taste, like lemon or vinegar
p1.example: Sour fruits grown fresh contain vitamins that have a positive effect on vision.
p1.ex1: She noticed the diet contained too many bitter and sour items rather than fresh produce.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, sour and bitter food items on sale still contain beneficial vitamins.

p1.en: the absence of light; the condition of there being no light
p1.example: A diet rich in vitamins allows the eyes to see better in the dark.
p1.ex1: Cutting down on junk food and going on a diet improves vision in the dark.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, the harmful effect of fatty food reduces the ability to see clearly in the dark.

p1.en: the ability to see; the quality of eyesight
p1.example: A diet rich in vitamins and fibre has a positive effect on vision and heart health.
p1.ex1: Cutting down on junk food allows the body to maintain better vision in the dark.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, the harmful amount of salty and fatty food affects vision negatively.

p1.en: a natural substance found in food that the body needs to stay healthy
p1.example: Fresh produce is rich in vitamins and has a positive effect on vision and heart health.
p1.ex1: Going on a diet rich in vitamins allows the body to produce energy and maintain good sight.
p1.ex2: Nowadays, junk food contains very few vitamins — harmful for the heart and vision.

p2.en: a grass crop like wheat, rice or oats; also a breakfast food made from grains
p2.example: Oatmeal cereal is rich in fibre and has a positive effect on heart health.
p2.ex1: She placed a bowl of cereal on the cover of the diet plan booklet.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and starting with a dairy product or cereal is beneficial.

p2.en: the outside of a book or magazine; also something that goes over another object
p2.example: The cover of the diet booklet showed fresh produce — no junk food items.
p2.ex1: She placed the sliced dairy product under a cover to keep it fresh.
p2.ex2: The recipe showed how to slice the broccoli and place it under a cover to steam.

p2.en: food made from milk, such as cheese, yoghurt or butter
p2.example: A diet that contains fresh dairy products is rich in vitamins and good for the heart.
p2.ex1: She placed sliced dairy products and cereal on the table as a healthy start.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, dairy products on sale contain less harm than fatty junk food items.

p2.en: to damage or hurt something; also the damage or injury caused
p2.example: Too much salty food harms the heart — cut down on harmful junk food items.
p2.ex1: She placed the diet plan to reduce harm from fatty and bitter food.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, the harm caused by junk food on vision and heart health is well known.

p2.en: to put something in a particular position
p2.example: She placed sliced broccoli and spinach in the bowl for the healthy diet.
p2.ex1: Place the cereal in a cover and add sliced dairy product for a rich start.
p2.ex2: The recipe advised to place coconut and mango on top of the oatmeal cereal.

p2.en: to cut something into thin flat pieces
p2.example: She sliced the cucumber and placed it beside the salmon and spinach.
p2.ex1: Slice the mango and pineapple and place them on the cover of the cereal bowl.
p2.ex2: The recipe showed how to slice garlic and add it to the broccoli and noodles.

p2.en: a green vegetable with tightly packed flower heads, rich in vitamins
p2.example: Broccoli is rich in vitamins and has a positive effect on vision and heart health.
p2.ex1: She sliced the broccoli and placed it beside the salmon and noodles.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, broccoli is one of the most beneficial items to add to a healthy diet.

p2.en: a large round green or white vegetable with layered leaves
p2.example: Cabbage is rich in fibre and vitamins — a great fresh item for any diet.
p2.ex1: She placed sliced cabbage beside the cucumber and garlic.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and adding cabbage to the diet has a positive effect.

p2.en: a large tropical fruit with a hard shell, white flesh and sweet juice
p2.example: She placed sliced coconut and mango on the cereal as a fresh and vitamin-rich start.
p2.ex1: Coconut contains a beneficial amount of vitamins and is rich in natural fibre.
p2.ex2: She sliced the coconut and added it to the pineapple and oatmeal bowl.

p2.en: a long green vegetable with a watery, mild taste
p2.example: She sliced the cucumber and placed it beside the salmon and spinach.
p2.ex1: A cucumber and cabbage salad is fresh and rich in vitamins — good for vision.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, cucumber is one of the most common fresh items added to a healthy diet.

p2.en: a strong-smelling plant used in cooking to add flavour
p2.example: She sliced the garlic and placed it with the broccoli and noodles.
p2.ex1: Garlic contains vitamins and has a positive effect on heart health.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and using garlic in cooking reduces harmful effects.

p2.en: small sweet or sour fruits that grow in clusters on a vine
p2.example: Grapes contain vitamins and are rich in fibre — a healthy addition to any diet.
p2.ex1: She placed fresh grapes beside the coconut and mango for a vitamin-rich start.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, grapes on sale contain a beneficial amount of vitamins and antioxidants.

p2.en: meat from a young sheep
p2.example: She placed sliced lamb beside the spinach and garlic for a nutritious dinner.
p2.ex1: A diet that contains lamb and broccoli is rich in vitamins and good for the heart.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, lamb is a healthy alternative to fatty junk food items.

p2.en: a sweet tropical fruit with orange flesh
p2.example: She sliced the mango and placed it with coconut and pineapple on the cereal.
p2.ex1: Mango is rich in vitamins and has a positive effect on vision and skin health.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and adding mango to the diet is a great fresh start.

p2.en: long thin strips of pasta or dough, used in Asian and Western cooking
p2.example: She placed the noodles beside sliced garlic and broccoli for a healthy meal.
p2.ex1: Noodles are a good alternative to fatty junk food when cooked with fresh produce.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, noodles with spinach and garlic are a common diet item rich in fibre.

p2.en: a food made from oats, usually eaten as porridge for breakfast
p2.example: Oatmeal is rich in fibre and vitamins — a great start to a healthy diet.
p2.ex1: She placed sliced mango and coconut on the oatmeal cereal.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and having oatmeal as a start has a positive effect on the heart.

p2.en: a soft sweet fruit with fuzzy skin and a stone inside
p2.example: She placed a sliced peach beside the grapes and pear for a vitamin-rich diet.
p2.ex1: Peaches are rich in vitamins and have a positive effect on vision.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, fresh peaches on sale contain more vitamins than processed food items.

p2.en: a sweet fruit with a rounded base and narrower top
p2.example: She sliced the pear and placed it with the peach and grapes as a fresh start.
p2.ex1: A pear is rich in fibre and vitamins — a great item for any healthy diet.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and having a pear as a snack reduces harmful effects.

p2.en: a large tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh
p2.example: She placed sliced pineapple and coconut on the oatmeal as a fresh vitamin-rich start.
p2.ex1: Pineapple contains vitamins and has a positive effect on digestion and vision.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, fresh pineapple on sale is rich in vitamins — much better than junk food.

p2.en: a large pink fish, rich in healthy fats and protein
p2.example: She placed sliced salmon beside the spinach and cucumber for a nutritious meal.
p2.ex1: Salmon is rich in vitamins and has a positive effect on heart health.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and having salmon on a diet reduces harmful effects.

p2.en: small shellfish used in cooking, usually pink when cooked
p2.example: She placed the shrimp beside the noodles and garlic for a light healthy dish.
p2.ex1: Shrimp contains vitamins and is a great low-fat item for a healthy diet.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, shrimp and salmon are among the most popular fresh items on sale.

p2.en: a dark green leafy vegetable rich in vitamins and iron
p2.example: Spinach is rich in vitamins and has a positive effect on vision and heart health.
p2.ex1: She placed sliced spinach beside the salmon and cucumber.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on junk food and adding spinach to the diet reduces harmful effects.

p2.en: a large bird or its meat, often used as a healthy alternative to fatty food
p2.example: She placed sliced turkey beside the broccoli and cabbage for a lean meal.
p2.ex1: Turkey is rich in protein and vitamins — a great item for a healthy diet.
p2.ex2: Nowadays, turkey is a popular alternative to fatty junk food items.

p3.en: to successfully reach a goal through effort
p3.example: She registered for the seminar to achieve her monthly fitness and diet goals.
p3.ex1: The climber contacted the noticeboard team to achieve registration for the qualified course.
p3.ex2: Wonder how to achieve better health? Firstly, register for the seminar and request a towel.

p3.en: a person who climbs rocks or mountains as a sport or activity
p3.example: The qualified climber contacted the seminar team via the noticeboard to register.
p3.ex1: She was unable to wonder at the monthly route — the climber registration was closed.
p3.ex2: Firstly, the climber requested a towel and contacted the noticeboard for registration details.

p3.en: to get in touch with someone by phone, email or letter
p3.example: Please contact us via the noticeboard to register for the monthly seminar.
p3.ex1: She was unable to achieve registration without contacting the qualified team.
p3.ex2: The climber contacted the seminar staff to request a towel and monthly schedule.

p3.en: a small piece of information; the finer points of something
p3.example: Please contact the noticeboard for details on the monthly seminar registration.
p3.ex1: She requested full details of the qualified course before registering.
p3.ex2: The climber wondered whether the detail on the noticeboard was up to date.

p3.en: happening once a month or every month
p3.example: The monthly seminar on healthy diet is listed on the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: She registered for the monthly session and contacted the qualified instructor.
p3.ex2: The climber requested a towel and contacted the team for monthly registration details.

p3.en: a board where notices and information are displayed publicly
p3.example: Details of the qualified seminar and registration are on the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: She contacted the team after reading the monthly seminar notice on the noticeboard.
p3.ex2: The climber wondered whether the registration detail on the noticeboard was correct.

p3.en: having the necessary skills, training or certificates for something
p3.example: The seminar was led by a qualified instructor — registration was via the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: She was unable to register without the approval of a qualified team member.
p3.ex2: Contact the qualified climber directly for monthly seminar details and registration.

p3.en: to officially sign up for something
p3.example: Please register for the monthly seminar via the noticeboard or contact the team.
p3.ex1: She was unable to achieve registration without contacting the qualified instructor.
p3.ex2: Firstly, register your details — then request a towel and contact the seminar team.

p3.en: the process of officially signing up for something
p3.example: Registration for the monthly seminar is via the noticeboard — contact us for details.
p3.ex1: She was unable to complete registration without a qualified instructor's approval.
p3.ex2: Firstly, check the noticeboard for registration details and contact the climber team.

p3.en: to formally ask for something
p3.example: Please request a towel and registration details via the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: She contacted the qualified team to request monthly seminar registration.
p3.ex2: The climber wondered whether to request more detail or simply contact the noticeboard.

p3.en: a meeting or class for discussion and learning on a particular topic
p3.example: The monthly seminar on healthy diet is led by a qualified instructor.
p3.ex1: She registered for the seminar after reading the detail on the noticeboard.
p3.ex2: Contact the team to request registration and a towel for the monthly seminar.

p3.en: a piece of cloth used for drying yourself after washing or exercise
p3.example: She registered for the seminar and requested a towel via the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: Contact the qualified team to request a towel for the monthly climbing session.
p3.ex2: The noticeboard listed registration details — bring a towel and contact the instructor.

p3.en: not having the ability or opportunity to do something
p3.example: She was unable to register for the seminar without contacting the noticeboard first.
p3.ex1: The climber was unable to achieve monthly registration without a qualified approval.
p3.ex2: She was unable to request a towel without first completing the registration detail.

p3.en: to think about something with curiosity or uncertainty
p3.example: She wondered whether to register for the monthly seminar via the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: The climber wondered whether the qualified instructor would contact her about registration.
p3.ex2: Wonder how to achieve your goals? Contact the seminar team and register today.

p3.en: a formal greeting used at the start of a letter or email when you don't know the recipient's name
p3.example: Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to register for the monthly seminar on the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: Dear Sir/Madam, I would like to request registration details from the qualified team.
p3.ex2: Dear Sir/Madam, I wonder whether it is possible to contact the climber instructor directly.

p3.word: I look forward to hearing from you.
p3.en: a polite closing phrase used in formal letters to say you expect a reply
p3.example: I look forward to hearing from you regarding my monthly seminar registration.
p3.ex1: I look forward to hearing from you with details of the qualified seminar on the noticeboard.
p3.ex2: Please send me a reply as soon as possible. I look forward to hearing from you.

p3.word: I would like to thank you in advance (for your help).
p3.en: a polite phrase expressing gratitude before receiving the help
p3.example: I would like to thank you in advance for your help with my seminar registration.
p3.ex1: Dear Sir/Madam, I would like to thank you in advance for sending the noticeboard detail.
p3.ex2: I would like to thank you in advance for contacting the qualified team on my behalf.

p3.word: Please send me a reply (with the information) as soon as possible.
p3.ru: Пожалуйста, пришлите мне ответ как можно скорее.
p3.en: a polite request for a prompt written response
p3.example: Please send me a reply with the registration detail as soon as possible.
p3.ex1: Please send me a reply with the qualified seminar schedule as soon as possible.
p3.ex2: Dear Sir/Madam, please send me a reply regarding monthly registration as soon as possible.

p3.en: a polite phrase thanking the reader for reading and responding
p3.example: Thank you for your time — I look forward to hearing from you about registration.
p3.ex1: Thank you for your time. Please send me the noticeboard detail as soon as possible.
p3.ex2: Dear Sir/Madam, thank you for your time and for contacting the qualified team.

p3.en: used to close a formal letter when you don't know the person's name
p3.example: Yours faithfully, [Name] — used when opening with Dear Sir/Madam.
p3.ex1: Yours faithfully — always used after Dear Sir/Madam in formal letters.
p3.ex2: She ended the registration letter with Yours faithfully before signing her name.

p3.en: used to close a formal letter when you know the person's name
p3.example: Yours sincerely, [Name] — used when opening with Dear Mr/Ms [Name].
p3.ex1: Yours sincerely — always used when you know the qualified instructor's name.
p3.ex2: She ended the monthly seminar letter with Yours sincerely after addressing the climber.

p3.en: used to introduce the last point in a series
p3.example: Finally, I would like to thank you in advance for your help with registration.
p3.ex1: Firstly, contact the noticeboard. Secondly, register. Finally, request a towel.
p3.ex2: Finally, please send me a reply as soon as possible — I look forward to hearing from you.

p3.en: used to introduce the first point in a list or sequence
p3.example: Firstly, I would like to register for the monthly seminar on the noticeboard.
p3.ex1: Firstly, contact the qualified team. Secondly, complete registration. Finally, request a towel.
p3.ex2: Firstly, I am writing to request detail about the seminar. I look forward to hearing from you.

p3.en: used to add more information to what has already been said
p3.example: In addition, I would like to request a towel for the monthly seminar.
p3.ex1: Firstly, register via the noticeboard. In addition, contact the qualified instructor.
p3.ex2: In addition, please send me a reply with all registration details as soon as possible.

p3.en: used to introduce the final point, similar to finally
p3.example: Lastly, I would like to thank you in advance for your help with registration.
p3.ex1: Firstly, contact. Secondly, register. Lastly, request a towel and wait for a reply.
p3.ex2: Lastly, I look forward to hearing from you about the monthly seminar detail.

p3.en: used to introduce the second point in a sequence
p3.example: Secondly, I would like to request more detail about the qualified seminar.
p3.ex1: Firstly, contact the noticeboard. Secondly, register. Finally, request a towel.
p3.ex2: Secondly, please send me a reply with the monthly schedule as soon as possible.

p3.en: used to introduce the first point, slightly more informal than firstly
p3.example: To begin with, I am writing to register for the monthly seminar.
p3.ex1: To begin with, I would like to contact the qualified team about noticeboard registration.
p3.ex2: To begin with, thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.

p3.en: used to add an important extra point, stronger than in addition
p3.example: What is more, I would like to request a towel for the monthly climbing seminar.
p3.ex1: Firstly, register. What is more, contact the qualified team for full noticeboard detail.
p3.ex2: What is more, please send me a reply as soon as possible — I look forward to hearing from you.

p1.en: To make a formal request for something such as a job, course or place
p1.example: She applied for a job after attending the careers fair.
p1.ex1: He applied for a place on the graduate training programme.
p1.ex2: You need to apply before the deadline with a complete CV.

p1.en: Used to describe the effect or outcome of a previous action
p1.example: As a result of her training, she received a high salary.
p1.ex1: He did not prepare his CV and as a result failed the interview.
p1.ex2: As a result of the warning, many employees chose to quit.

p1.en: Used to say the right moment for doing something has arrived
p1.example: It was time to move on and find a better career option.
p1.ex1: She felt it was time to apply for a higher position.
p1.ex2: He decided it was time to quit and try something completely new.

p1.en: A person who applies for a job, place on a course or position
p1.example: She was clearly the strongest candidate at the careers fair.
p1.ex1: The director interviewed five candidates for the new role.
p1.ex2: He was a strong candidate with impressive qualifications.

p1.en: A possible job or profession that someone might choose to pursue
p1.example: Teaching is a very popular career option among graduates.
p1.ex1: She explored several career options at the careers fair.
p1.ex2: The workshop helped students understand different career options.

p1.en: An event where employers and job seekers meet to discuss opportunities
p1.example: She attended a careers fair and found an excellent career option.
p1.ex1: The university organised a careers fair for all final-year students.
p1.ex2: He spoke to several potential employers at the careers fair.

p1.en: A particular situation or example of something happening
p1.example: In this case, work experience matters more than qualifications.
p1.ex1: She made a strong case for receiving a higher salary.
p1.ex2: The warning was made very clear in each individual case.

p1.en: A document listing a person's education, experience and skills
p1.example: She updated her CV carefully before attending the careers fair.
p1.ex1: He sent his CV to several companies and received an interview.
p1.ex2: A good CV should always include your qualifications and work experience.

p1.en: A person who is in charge of and manages a company or organisation
p1.example: The director gave a presentation about the company's future plans.
p1.ex1: She became a director after twenty years of successful employment.
p1.ex2: He was the director who managed the graduate training programme.

p1.en: Politely used to describe people who are quite old in age
p1.example: She gained valuable experience working with elderly people.
p1.ex1: The programme was designed to help elderly employees retire comfortably.
p1.ex2: He managed a team that provided care for elderly patients.

p1.en: A person who is paid to work for a company or organisation
p1.example: The director praised every employee warmly at the presentation.
p1.ex1: She was a long-term employee with very high qualifications.
p1.ex2: Employees received a warning before the company shut down.

p1.en: The state of having a paid job; the activity of working
p1.example: Employment opportunities increased as a direct result of the programme.
p1.ex1: He found full-time employment after attending the careers fair.
p1.ex2: The warning led many people to look urgently for new employment.

p1.en: To be real or present in the world at a particular time
p1.example: Career options that exist today may not exist for years to come.
p1.ex1: The training programme has existed successfully for over twenty years.
p1.ex2: No warning existed at all before the company suddenly shut down.

p1.en: For a long and extended period of time in the future
p1.example: This qualification will be extremely useful for years to come.
p1.ex1: She planned her career goals carefully for years to come.
p1.ex2: The director hoped the programme would succeed for years to come.

p1.en: Describing something or someone that existed or held a role in the past
p1.example: The former director gave a fascinating presentation at the fair.
p1.ex1: She met her former colleague unexpectedly at the workshop.
p1.ex2: He was a former employee who had chosen to move on.

p1.en: To get or acquire something useful or valuable over time
p1.example: She gained valuable work experience during the graduate programme.
p1.ex1: He gained a high salary after getting additional qualifications.
p1.ex2: You can gain important skills by attending a training workshop.

p1.en: All the people born and living at around the same period of time
p1.example: The new generation of employees has very strong technical skills.
p1.ex1: She represented the generation that moved on from traditional careers.
p1.ex2: For years to come, this generation will lead major employment trends.

p1.en: A person who has successfully completed a university degree
p1.example: She graduated from university and immediately attended a careers fair.
p1.ex1: He was a graduate with excellent qualifications and experience.
p1.ex2: Graduates often need relevant work experience to gain a high salary.

p1.en: Greater than normal in amount, degree or level
p1.example: She received a very high salary after her well-deserved promotion.
p1.ex1: The director set a high standard for every employee.
p1.ex2: High qualifications significantly increase your chances of employment.

p1.en: To become or make something greater in amount, size or level
p1.example: Her salary increased significantly as a result of the training.
p1.ex1: Employment in the sector increased dramatically last year.
p1.ex2: The number of candidates at the careers fair increased every year.

p1.en: To be in charge of something or to guide and direct others
p1.example: She was chosen to lead the new graduate training programme.
p1.ex1: He led the impressive presentation at the careers fair.
p1.ex2: The director leads a large team of highly experienced employees.

p1.en: To be responsible for or control something; to succeed at doing something
p1.example: She manages a team of twenty dedicated employees every day.
p1.ex1: He managed to gain a high salary in his former role.
p1.ex2: The director managed the careers fair workshop very efficiently.

p1.en: To leave a job or situation and progress to something new
p1.example: She decided to move on and look for better career options.
p1.ex1: He moved on from his former employer to a technical college.
p1.ex2: As a result of the warning, many employees chose to move on.

p1.en: Not any more; used to say something has stopped or ended
p1.example: She no longer works at the company after it shut down.
p1.ex1: He no longer needed a warning to take decisive action.
p1.ex2: The former director no longer leads the training programme.

p1.en: Used to introduce the first of two contrasting points or ideas
p1.example: On the one hand, a high salary is very important in a career.
p1.ex1: On the one hand, work experience helps you gain many skills.
p1.ex2: On the one hand, the careers fair offered many valuable options.

p1.en: Used to introduce the second of two contrasting points or ideas
p1.example: On the other hand, a good work environment matters even more.
p1.ex1: On the other hand, qualifications alone are simply not enough.
p1.ex2: On the other hand, the warning was ignored by too many people.

p1.en: A position on a course, at an institution or in an organisation
p1.example: She got a place on the graduate training programme.
p1.ex1: He applied for a place at a well-known technical college.
p1.ex2: There were only ten places available at the workshop.

p1.en: A formal talk given to a group of people, often with visual aids
p1.example: She gave a presentation about career options at the fair.
p1.ex1: The director's presentation impressed every single candidate present.
p1.ex2: He spent hours preparing a presentation for the important workshop.

p1.en: A planned series of activities or events designed for a specific purpose
p1.example: She joined a graduate training programme after completing university.
p1.ex1: The employment programme helped thousands of people find work.
p1.ex2: He managed the careers fair programme on behalf of the director.

p1.en: An official certificate or skill gained through study or experience
p1.example: She gained excellent qualifications at a well-known technical college.
p1.ex1: High qualifications increase your chances significantly in employment.
p1.ex2: His former employer valued practical work experience over qualifications.

p1.en: To leave a job, stop doing something or give something up
p1.example: She quit her job to move on and explore better career options.
p1.ex1: He quit the programme as a direct result of the warning.
p1.ex2: The former director quit after many long years of employment.

p1.en: Correct or most suitable for a particular person or situation
p1.example: She made the right decision to attend the careers fair.
p1.ex1: He applied for the right job after gaining relevant work experience.
p1.ex2: A well-prepared CV is the right way to get a high salary.

p1.en: A fixed amount of money paid regularly to an employed person
p1.example: She negotiated a very high salary at the job interview.
p1.ex1: His salary increased significantly as a result of the training programme.
p1.ex2: The former director earned the highest salary in the company.

p1.en: To stop operating completely, either permanently or for a period
p1.example: The company shut down as a result of serious financial trouble.
p1.ex1: Several technical colleges shut down unexpectedly last year.
p1.ex2: The director shut down the programme as a result of the warning.

p1.en: A person who gives a formal talk or address to an audience
p1.example: The main speaker at the careers fair was a former director.
p1.ex1: She was invited as the keynote speaker for the workshop.
p1.ex2: The speaker gave a fascinating presentation about employment trends.

p1.en: To achieve what you wanted or intended to do
p1.example: She succeeded in gaining a place on the training programme.
p1.ex1: He succeeded as a direct result of his hard work and qualifications.
p1.ex2: The former director hoped the programme would succeed for years.

p1.en: A college that offers practical and vocational training programmes
p1.example: She studied at a technical college before starting university.
p1.ex1: He gained all his qualifications at a local technical college.
p1.ex2: The technical college organised a successful careers fair every year.

p1.en: The process of learning the skills needed for a particular job
p1.example: She completed a training programme before starting her new job.
p1.ex1: His salary increased significantly as a result of the training.
p1.ex2: The director organised a training workshop for all new employees.

p1.en: A problem or difficulty that causes inconvenience or worry
p1.example: The company was in serious financial trouble before it shut down.
p1.ex1: She had real trouble writing her CV for the careers fair.
p1.ex2: As a result of the trouble, many employees decided to quit.

p1.en: A statement informing someone about possible danger or problems
p1.example: She received an urgent warning before the company shut down.
p1.ex1: The director issued a formal warning to all employees.
p1.ex2: The warning led many people to search urgently for new employment.

p1.en: Time spent working in a job to learn about it, often unpaid
p1.example: She gained valuable work experience before attending the careers fair.
p1.ex1: He included all his work experience carefully on his CV.
p1.ex2: Work experience is highly important for gaining good qualifications.

p1.en: A meeting or session where people learn and discuss a topic together
p1.example: She attended a very useful workshop about CV writing.
p1.ex1: The director ran a workshop for all newly employed staff.
p1.ex2: The workshop at the careers fair was extremely informative.

p2.en: A strong desire to achieve something or to be very successful
p2.example: She had a great ambition to become a company director one day.
p2.ex1: His ambition drove him to gain the highest qualifications possible.
p2.ex2: Without ambition it is very difficult to succeed in employment.

p2.en: To be absent from home or work for a period of time
p2.example: She was away for a week attending an important training programme.
p2.ex1: He was away at a careers fair and missed the warning.
p2.ex2: The director was away when the company suddenly shut down.

p2.en: A car provided by an employer for an employee to use for work
p2.example: She received a company car as part of her employment package.
p2.ex1: One of the benefits of the job was a free company car.
p2.ex2: He used his company car to travel to the careers fair.

p2.en: A problem or something that is not easy to deal with or do
p2.example: She had real difficulty finding the right career option for her.
p2.ex1: As a result of the difficulty, he decided to quit the programme.
p2.ex2: The director had difficulty managing the large and complex workshop.

p2.en: To leave a course, activity or competition before completing it
p2.example: He dropped out of the training programme after just one month.
p2.ex1: She nearly dropped out but carried on and eventually succeeded.
p2.ex2: Several candidates dropped out before the entrance exam results.

p2.en: To receive money in return for work that you do for someone
p2.example: She earns a very high salary as a result of her qualifications.
p2.ex1: He wanted to earn more money by gaining entirely new skills.
p2.ex2: You can earn significantly more if you gain relevant work experience.

p2.en: A person or company that pays other people to work for them
p2.example: She greatly impressed her employer at the job presentation.
p2.ex1: He found a new employer after attending the careers fair.
p2.ex2: A good employer always provides proper training and good conditions.

p2.en: A test you must pass in order to get into a school or college
p2.example: She prepared very hard for the entrance exam at the technical college.
p2.ex1: He failed the entrance exam and dropped out of the programme.
p2.ex2: Good qualifications improve your chances greatly in an entrance exam.

p2.en: To try hard to achieve or obtain something you really want
p2.example: She decided to go after her ambition of becoming a director.
p2.ex1: He went after a high salary by gaining additional qualifications.
p2.ex2: Go after the career option that suits your personal goals best.

p2.en: Something important that you are trying hard to achieve
p2.example: Her goal was to gain a place on the graduate programme.
p2.ex1: He set a clear goal to earn a high salary within five years.
p2.ex2: The careers fair helped her finally decide on her career goal.

p2.en: To have a plan or firm purpose to do something in the future
p2.example: She intended to apply for a place at a technical college.
p2.ex1: He intended to move on after gaining enough relevant experience.
p2.ex2: The director intended to make the programme succeed.

p2.en: Ordinary or usual; what is typically expected in a given situation
p2.example: It is completely normal to feel nervous before an entrance exam.
p2.ex1: She moved on when her work situation was no longer normal.
p2.ex2: High qualifications are now considered normal for most career options.

p2.en: Working or happening for only part of the standard working hours
p2.example: She worked part-time while studying hard for her qualifications.
p2.ex1: He took a part-time job to gain some useful work experience.
p2.ex2: Part-time employment helped her manage both work and her studies.

p2.en: Lasting for a long time or intended to continue indefinitely
p2.example: She was offered a permanent position after completing the training.
p2.ex1: He moved on from a temporary job to permanent employment.
p2.ex2: A permanent contract means a stable salary for years to come.

p2.en: Relating to a particular person and not to others
p2.example: She described her personal goals clearly in the job presentation.
p2.ex1: His personal ambition was to become a company director.
p2.ex2: Personal qualities are just as important as formal qualifications.

p2.en: Happening or existing before the present or current one
p2.example: She listed all her previous employment carefully on her CV.
p2.ex1: His previous employer had offered him a very high salary.
p2.ex2: The previous director left an important warning for the new team.

p2.en: The state of not having a paid job; the number of people without work
p2.example: As a result of the shutdown, unemployment increased significantly.
p2.ex1: She studied hard to avoid unemployment after her graduation.
p2.ex2: The careers fair was organised specifically to help reduce unemployment.

p2.en: Probable (likely) or improbable (unlikely) to happen or be true
p2.example: It is unlikely that she will quit her well-paid job so soon.
p2.ex1: It is likely that employment will increase as a result of the programme.
p2.ex2: It is unlikely that high qualifications alone will guarantee success.

p2.en: Money paid to a worker, often weekly or calculated by hours worked
p2.example: He earned a very low wage at his temporary job.
p2.ex1: She hoped to increase her wage by gaining new qualifications.
p2.ex2: A high wage is a very common goal for many job candidates.

p2.en: Working the standard number of hours every week in a paid job
p2.example: She found full-time employment after completing the training programme.
p2.ex1: He moved from part-time to full-time employment last year.
p2.ex2: Full-time employment provides a stable and permanent salary.

p2.en: The formal process of applying for a job at a company
p2.example: She spent hours carefully preparing her job application and CV.
p2.ex1: He submitted his job application at the careers fair.
p2.ex2: A strong job application includes qualifications and work experience.

p2.en: A job that does not pay very much money to the employee
p2.example: He had a low-paid job before gaining his important qualifications.
p2.ex1: She quit her low-paid job to pursue a better career option.
p2.ex2: A low-paid job can still provide very useful work experience.

p2.en: A job that lasts for only a limited and fixed period of time
p2.example: She took a temporary job while looking for permanent employment.
p2.ex1: He moved on from his temporary job to permanent employment.
p2.ex2: A temporary job helped him gain valuable work experience.

p2.en: A job that pays a good or high amount of money to the employee
p2.example: Her main goal was to find a well-paid job after graduation.
p2.ex1: He gained qualifications to increase his chances of a well-paid job.
p2.ex2: A well-paid job usually requires high qualifications and experience.

p2.en: The conditions and atmosphere in which an employee works daily
p2.example: A positive work environment helps all employees succeed together.
p2.ex1: She chose the company specifically for its excellent work environment.
p2.ex2: The director improved the work environment after the warning.

p2.en: The physical and practical circumstances in which someone works
p2.example: Good working conditions are just as important as a high salary.
p2.ex1: She quit because the working conditions were no longer acceptable.
p2.ex2: Employees have a right to safe and fair working conditions.

p2.en: The hours during which an employee is required to work
p2.example: She negotiated her working hours carefully before accepting the job.
p2.ex1: Long working hours led several employees to quit their jobs.
p2.ex2: Part-time employees have shorter working hours than full-time staff.

p1.en: A personal profile or record on a website or online service
p1.example: She created an account on the learning platform.
p1.ex1: He checked his account before submitting the assignment.
p1.ex2: You need an account to access the newsfeed.

p1.en: Except for something; in addition to something
p1.example: Apart from the virus, the program worked well.
p1.ex1: Apart from the keyboard, she needed a new mouse.
p1.ex2: Apart from uploading the assignment, she also posted feedback.

p1.en: A piece of work given to a student or employee to complete
p1.example: She had to hand in her assignment before the deadline.
p1.ex1: He uploaded the assignment to the learning platform.
p1.ex2: The teacher gave detailed feedback on every assignment.

p1.en: To connect a file to an email or message for sending
p1.example: She attached her CV to the covering email.
p1.ex1: He forgot to attach the assignment before sending it.
p1.ex2: You can attach a file by clicking the button.

p1.en: A small object you press or click to make something happen
p1.example: Click the button to upload your assignment to the platform.
p1.ex1: She pressed the wrong button and accidentally deleted the file.
p1.ex2: The restart button is at the top of the keyboard.

p1.en: To put electricity into a battery so a device can be used
p1.example: She forgot to charge her laptop before the lesson.
p1.ex1: He charged the device overnight before the presentation.
p1.ex2: Remember to charge your keyboard before the important meeting.

p1.en: To press a button on a mouse or screen to select something
p1.example: Click the button to restart the program.
p1.ex1: She clicked on the link and it accidentally installed a virus.
p1.ex2: He clicked the wrong page and lost his entire assignment.

p1.en: Easy to use and fitting in well with your needs or schedule
p1.example: The platform is very convenient for submitting assignments.
p1.ex1: She found it convenient to upload her work from home.
p1.ex2: An electronic timetable is convenient for all students.

p1.en: To permanently remove information or a file from a computer
p1.example: She accidentally deleted her assignment before handing it in.
p1.ex1: He deleted the virus from the program successfully.
p1.ex2: Do not delete that file — it contains your important feedback.

p1.en: A conversation where people talk about a topic in detail
p1.example: She started a discussion on the platform about the assignment.
p1.ex1: The teacher gave feedback after the group discussion.
p1.ex2: He posted his ideas in the online discussion thread.

p1.en: Relating to devices or systems that use electricity and digital technology
p1.example: She submitted her assignment by electronic means.
p1.ex1: The electronic timetable was updated on the platform.
p1.ex2: He received detailed electronic feedback from his teacher.

p1.en: To type information into a computer; or to go into a place
p1.example: She entered her password to access the account.
p1.ex1: He entered the wrong details and got locked out.
p1.ex2: Enter your details and click the button to continue.

p1.en: Comments given about someone's work to help them improve
p1.example: The teacher gave detailed feedback on every assignment.
p1.ex1: She posted feedback on the discussion platform.
p1.ex2: He read the electronic feedback and improved his work.

p1.en: To give a completed piece of work to a teacher or supervisor
p1.example: She handed in her assignment right on time.
p1.ex1: He forgot to hand in his work and received a warning.
p1.ex2: Please hand in your assignment before the deadline.

p1.en: To put a program or application onto a computer so it can be used
p1.example: She installed the program on her new laptop.
p1.ex1: He installed the wrong version and it caused a virus.
p1.ex2: You need to install the software before you can start.

p1.en: A set of keys used to type and enter information into a computer
p1.example: She typed her assignment using the keyboard.
p1.ex1: His keyboard stopped working after the virus.
p1.ex2: The keyboard is connected to the platform device.

p1.en: To prevent access to something using a key or password
p1.example: She locked her account to keep it completely secure.
p1.ex1: The screen locks automatically after a few minutes of inactivity.
p1.ex2: He forgot his password and got locked out of his account.

p1.en: A small device used to move the cursor and click on a screen
p1.example: She used the mouse to scroll through the newsfeed.
p1.ex1: He clicked the button using the mouse.
p1.ex2: Apart from the mouse, the keyboard also stopped working.

p1.en: A constantly updated list of posts and updates on a platform
p1.example: She scrolled through the newsfeed and saw the post.
p1.ex1: He posted a discussion topic on the newsfeed.
p1.ex2: The newsfeed showed all the latest updates from the platform.

p1.en: Having things planned and arranged neatly and efficiently
p1.example: She was very organised and always handed in assignments on time.
p1.ex1: He kept his electronic files organised on the platform.
p1.ex2: An organised student manages their timetable well.

p1.en: A single document or section on a website
p1.example: She found the information on the wrong page.
p1.ex1: He bookmarked the platform's main page.
p1.ex2: Click the button on the page to upload your assignment.

p1.en: A secret word or code used to access an account or device
p1.example: She forgot her password and got locked out of her account.
p1.ex1: He entered his password and clicked the button to log in.
p1.ex2: Never share your password with anyone else.

p1.en: To insert text or an image that has been copied to another place
p1.example: She copied the text and pasted it into the assignment.
p1.ex1: He pasted the wrong file into the covering email.
p1.ex2: Select the text, copy it and then paste it into the page.

p1.en: An online service or system used to share, post or manage content
p1.example: She submitted her assignment on the learning platform.
p1.ex1: He posted his feedback in the online discussion platform.
p1.ex2: The platform is very convenient and easy to use.

p1.en: A message or piece of content shared online on a platform
p1.example: She wrote a post about the discussion topic.
p1.ex1: He read every post on the newsfeed carefully.
p1.ex2: The teacher's post included feedback on the assignment.

p1.en: To push a button or key firmly with your finger
p1.example: Press the button to restart the program.
p1.ex1: She pressed the wrong key and deleted the file.
p1.ex2: He pressed enter after typing in his password.

p1.en: A machine connected to a computer that produces paper copies
p1.example: She printed her assignment on the printer.
p1.ex1: The printer ran out of paper before she could hand in her work.
p1.ex2: He installed the printer program on his new laptop.

p1.en: A set of instructions that makes a computer perform a task
p1.example: She installed a new program to organise her timetable.
p1.ex1: The virus corrupted the program on his laptop.
p1.ex2: He deleted the old program and installed a better one.

p1.en: To a fairly large degree; more than a little but not completely
p1.example: She found the assignment quite difficult at first.
p1.ex1: The new platform is quite convenient to use.
p1.ex2: He was quite organised in managing his electronic timetable.

p1.en: To turn a device off and then on again to fix a problem
p1.example: She restarted her laptop after the virus appeared.
p1.ex1: He restarted the program by pressing the button.
p1.ex2: Try restarting the device if it does not respond.

p1.en: To move up or down through content displayed on a screen
p1.example: She scrolled through the newsfeed to find the post.
p1.ex1: He scrolled down the page to read the feedback.
p1.ex2: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click the button.

p1.en: To choose something from a list or group of available options
p1.example: She selected the file before clicking the upload button.
p1.ex1: He selected the wrong program from the platform.
p1.ex2: Select your assignment and click the button to hand it in.

p1.en: A device that produces sound from a computer or phone
p1.example: She turned up the speaker to hear the feedback clearly.
p1.ex1: He connected his speaker to the platform for the presentation.
p1.ex2: Apart from the keyboard, the speaker also needs charging.

p1.en: A schedule showing when events, classes or activities take place
p1.example: She checked the electronic timetable for the assignment deadline.
p1.ex1: He uploaded the new timetable to the platform.
p1.ex2: The timetable was convenient and easy to access online.

p1.en: Used to introduce an honest opinion that may surprise someone
p1.example: To be honest, she found the platform quite difficult at first.
p1.ex1: To be honest, the feedback was not very helpful.
p1.ex2: To be honest, he was not organised enough to hand in on time.

p1.en: To write something by pressing the keys on a keyboard
p1.example: She typed her assignment and uploaded it to the platform.
p1.ex1: He typed his password but the account remained locked.
p1.ex2: Type your details into the box and press enter.

p1.en: To send a file from your device to a website or platform
p1.example: She uploaded her assignment to the platform before the deadline.
p1.ex1: He uploaded the wrong file and had to delete and restart.
p1.ex2: Click the button to upload your document to the page.

p1.en: A harmful program that can damage or infect a computer's files
p1.example: The virus deleted several files from her program.
p1.ex1: He clicked on a link and installed a virus by mistake.
p1.ex2: She restarted her laptop to remove the virus.

p2.en: To be the right size or shape; to be suitable for a purpose
p2.example: The new program fits his working style very well.
p2.ex1: She found a job that fits her qualifications perfectly.
p2.ex2: Apart from the salary, the job fits all her requirements.

p2.en: To be defeated in a sports game or competition
p2.example: He was disappointed when his team lost the match.
p2.ex1: She lost the match but was proud of her performance.
p2.ex2: The team lost the match because they missed too many chances.

p2.en: To stop communicating with someone gradually over time
p2.example: She lost contact with her former colleague after he moved.
p2.ex1: He lost contact with his employer after the company shut down.
p2.ex2: Do not lose contact with your network after the careers fair.

p2.en: To stop being interested in something you once enjoyed or cared about
p2.example: She lost interest in the assignment after getting negative feedback.
p2.ex1: He lost interest in the platform when it became too difficult.
p2.ex2: Do not lose interest in your goal because of one bad result.

p2.en: To have less money than before because of spending or failure
p2.example: He lost money when the company shut down.
p2.ex1: She lost money by investing in the wrong programme.
p2.ex2: The business lost money as a result of the long shutdown.

p2.en: To stop having a paid job because you are dismissed or made redundant
p2.example: She lost her job when the company suddenly shut down.
p2.ex1: He lost his job and had to find new employment right away.
p2.ex2: As a result of the shutdown, many employees lost their jobs.

p2.en: To become less heavy; to reduce your body weight over time
p2.example: She decided to lose weight by jogging every morning.
p2.ex1: He lost weight during the exhausting expedition.
p2.ex2: You can lose weight by eating well and exercising regularly.

p2.en: To fail to attend a scheduled lesson or class
p2.example: She missed a class and fell behind with her assignment.
p2.ex1: He missed a class and asked a colleague for the feedback.
p2.ex2: Do not miss a class during the training programme.

p2.en: To arrive too late to board an aeroplane
p2.example: She missed her flight because she forgot to charge her device.
p2.ex1: He missed his flight to the careers fair.
p2.ex2: They missed a flight and had to find a new connection.

p2.en: To fail to attend or participate in a sports game
p2.example: He missed the match because of an injury to his ankle.
p2.ex1: She missed a match as a result of her illness.
p2.ex2: He was very disappointed to miss the important match.

p2.en: To fail to attend a scheduled meeting or appointment
p2.example: She missed the meeting because of a virus on her device.
p2.ex1: He missed his appointment with the director.
p2.ex2: Do not miss a meeting during the training programme.

p2.en: To not eat a meal at its normal or expected time
p2.example: She missed breakfast because she was late for the careers fair.
p2.ex1: He missed lunch to finish the assignment on time.
p2.ex2: Do not miss breakfast — it is the most important meal of the day.

p2.en: To feel sad because you are separated from your family
p2.example: She missed her family during the long training programme.
p2.ex1: He missed his family when he was away on the expedition.
p2.ex2: It is completely normal to miss your family when you work abroad.

p2.en: To fail to take an opportunity when it is your turn to act
p2.example: She missed her turn in the discussion because she was scrolling.
p2.ex1: He missed his turn at the presentation.
p2.ex2: Do not miss your turn to hand in the assignment.

p2.en: Immediately; without any delay whatsoever
p2.example: She uploaded the assignment right away after finishing it.
p2.ex1: He restarted the device right away when the virus appeared.
p2.ex2: Click the button right away to avoid losing your work.

p2.en: A person whose job is to manage financial accounts and records
p2.example: She works as an accountant at a large company.
p2.ex1: The accountant checked all the financial records carefully.
p2.ex2: He trained as an accountant after graduating from university.

p2.en: A person whose job is to construct or repair buildings and structures
p2.example: The builder completed the project on time and within budget.
p2.ex1: She hired a builder to repair the damaged roof.
p2.ex2: He worked as a builder before training to become a plumber.

p2.en: A person whose job is to stop fires and rescue people from danger
p2.example: The firefighter acted right away to save the building.
p2.ex1: She trained as a firefighter after leaving secondary school.
p2.ex2: Firefighters need to be physically fit and very experienced.

p2.en: A person whose job is to cut and style people's hair
p2.example: She works as a hairdresser in a local salon.
p2.ex1: The hairdresser was very experienced and creative.
p2.ex2: He trained as a hairdresser after dropping out of college.

p2.en: A person whose job is to advise people about the law
p2.example: She became a lawyer after gaining her qualifications.
p2.ex1: The lawyer gave advice about the employment contract.
p2.ex2: He trained as a lawyer at a well-known university.

p2.en: A person whose job is to keep swimmers safe at a pool or beach
p2.example: She worked as a lifeguard at the local swimming pool.
p2.ex1: The lifeguard acted right away when the swimmer was in danger.
p2.ex2: He trained as a lifeguard every summer during university.

p2.en: A person whose job is to install and repair water pipes and systems
p2.example: She called a plumber to fix the broken pipe.
p2.ex1: The plumber arrived right away and fixed the problem.
p2.ex2: He trained as a plumber at a local technical college.

p2.en: A person whose job is to protect a building or place from danger
p2.example: He works as a security guard at a large company.
p2.ex1: The security guard locked the building at night.
p2.ex2: She became a security guard after leaving her previous job.

p2.en: To block the path or progress of someone
p2.example: The printer was in her way when she tried to reach the keyboard.
p2.ex1: He was in her way during the important presentation.
p2.ex2: Do not be in the way — let her hand in the assignment first.

p2.en: To be familiar with a place or system and able to navigate it well
p2.example: She knows her way around the platform very well.
p2.ex1: He knew his way around the careers fair after attending last year.
p2.ex2: It takes time to know your way around a new work environment.

p2.en: To get lost; to stop knowing where you are going
p2.example: She lost her way to the careers fair.
p2.ex1: He lost his way in the new and unfamiliar company.
p2.ex2: Do not lose your way — follow the sign.

p2.en: While travelling or moving towards a particular destination
p2.example: She uploaded the assignment on her way to the library.
p2.ex1: He checked the newsfeed on his way to the careers fair.
p2.ex2: She messaged her employer on her way to the interview.

p2.en: Used to say something is impossible or to refuse something firmly
p2.example: There is no way she will miss the deadline again.
p2.ex1: No way can he hand in the assignment late.
p2.ex2: There is no way to restart the program without the password.

p3.en: At a high level of knowledge, skill or development
p3.example: She has an advanced knowledge of computer programs.
p3.ex1: He is looking for a candidate with advanced qualifications.
p3.ex2: The job requires an advanced level of English.

p3.en: A person who formally applies for a job or place on a course
p3.example: She was the most qualified applicant at the careers fair.
p3.ex1: The director interviewed ten applicants for the position.
p3.ex2: Every applicant must submit a CV and a covering email.

p3.en: At the current time; right now
p3.example: At present, she is working as a travel agent.
p3.ex1: He is at present completing an advanced training programme.
p3.ex2: At present, the position has not been filled.

p3.en: Forming the most important or simplest part of something
p3.example: She has basic computer skills and wants to improve them.
p3.ex1: The job requires at least a basic knowledge of the industry.
p3.ex2: He completed a basic training programme before applying.

p3.en: To be responsible for managing or looking after something
p3.example: She is in charge of the tourist office in the city.
p3.ex1: He was in charge of the training programme for new staff.
p3.ex2: The team leader is in charge of all working conditions.
